title: Quantization slope propagator and kernel handshake protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce per-layer dequant and precision-handoff overhead by introducing a minimal 'slope propagator' metadata channel plus a lightweight kernel handshake protocol that allows adjacent kernels to negotiate precision, avoid redundant dequant casts, and hand off KV cache fragments without full materialization. This ticket covers the runtime API changes, kernel-side microhooks, and fallbacks for models that require strict bit-exact behavior.
background: Our current unified execution path inserts materialized dequant casts between INT8/FP8 kernels and FP32 downstream operators. That pattern simplifies correctness but increases per-layer decode latency and memory traffic for low-latency streaming workloads (most visible at short to mid sequence lengths). Recent microbenchmarks show an average dequant materialization cost of ~0.7-1.0ms per attention layer at seq=256 on A100. We need a lower-friction mechanism to propagate quantization parameters and allow kernels to operate cooperatively.
proposed_solution: Add a compact per-request 'slope propagator' header in the runtime request context that carries per-tensor quant params (scale, zero-point, format-tag) and a small capability bitmask.

Expose a kernel handshake prelude: kernels implement two microhooks -- can_accept_precision(capabilities) and commit_handoff(metadata_ptr) -- invoked by the scheduler during prefill and decode to decide zero-copy or staged-materialize paths.
Implement a lightweight in-memory 'kv-fragment' descriptor so attention prefill can hand partial KV shards across kernel boundaries without coercing to FP32 unless strictly required.
Provide a deterministic fallback path: if any kernel in the chain lacks the capability bits, fall back to existing materialize-and-dequant route (preserve bit-exactness for critical models).
Add telemetry flags to trace successful handshake paths vs fallback to help ops tune quantization profiles per model.
Ship a user-facing opt-in flag (runtime config: quant_handshake=auto|on|off) that defaults to auto and only enables handshake when perf is observed to be beneficial in early experiments.
Deliver microbenchmarks and an end-to-end regression test suite to ensure numeric regressions are expected or documented.
Coordinate with model onboarding to add golden prompts to the eval suite for models that may be sensitive to quantization handoffs.
Phased rollout: start in dedicated dev clusters behind feature flag, then limited ramp to hosted canary customers, then broader rollout.
Document kernel developer guidelines and an ABI stability note for third-party kernels.
Estimated non-blocking implementation: 2 sprints for core runtime + 1 sprint for kernel adapters + 1 sprint for tests/rollout monitoring.
Ensure compatibility with existing per-model quant profiles and Optimize recommendations so customers can get suggestions without manual changes.
design_decisions: Prefer a tiny metadata channel over broad scheduler changes to minimize the blast radius of the feature.
Handshake implemented synchronously during prefill path for deterministic behavior; decode path uses cached handshake results to avoid repeated negotiation per token.
Represent quant params as fixed-width fields to keep the header <= 64 bytes in typical cases.
Fallback paths must preserve existing semantics for any model with strict numeric expectations; handshake is opt-in at config level until sign-off.
Telemetry will record handshake success rate, average avoided materializations per request, and any numeric-violation incidents (for audit).
Do not change public API surface for customers who do not opt into quant_handshake; behavior remains backward compatible.
Prefer conservative default capabilities for kernels: only advertise zero-copy-safe operations after local unit tests and perf validation.
Kernel handshake is versioned to allow iterative expansion (handshake_v1 contains scale/format; handshake_v2 may include sparse-layout hints).
Avoid cross-tenant kernel sharing of ephemeral descriptors; handshake metadata is per-request and ephemeral to satisfy privacy/audit constraints.
tradeoffs: Pros: Reduced memory traffic, lower per-layer latency for streaming; enables chained zero-copy execution for quantized pipelines.
Cons: Adds complexity to kernel authors and the scheduler; risk of subtle numeric differences if kernels misimplement capability guarantees.
Operational: Requires telemetry and careful rollout to detect models that observe quality regressions; may delay full rollout for regulated customers.
Engineering effort: non-trivial kernel changes across the kernel catalog; requirement to maintain deterministic fallback increases test burden.
benchmark_plan: Baseline: existing materialize-and-dequant path measured on A100 and T4 for seq lengths: 64, 128, 256, 512; measure p50/p90/p99 latency and memory bandwidth per-request.
Spike: implement handshake prototype for attention and ffn kernels and measure delta; target >=20% reduction in per-layer dequant overhead at seq<=256 for common LLMs (Llama2-13B, MPT-30B).
Microbench scripts: runtime-perf-bench repo, script quant-handshake/bench.sh with deterministic seeds and CPU pinning.
Run CI microbench comparisons on PRs; gate merge on non-regression for bit-exact models in 'strict-numeric' label group.
Collect telemetry over canary and compare customer-level QPS and error rates before full rollout.
Define performance targets: reduce decode stage wall-time by at least 0.15ms per attention layer at seq=128 on p50 for INT8 pipelines on A100.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flagged integration in dev clusters with handshake_v1 disabled by default; smoke tests only.
Phase 1: enable quant_handshake=on for internal staging workloads and run overnight perf sweep; collect telemetry for 48h.
Phase 2: enable on small subset of hosted canary customers (opt-in list) and Dedicated dev tenants; monitor quality regressions and rollback on incidents.
Phase 3: expand to broader pool with quant_handshake=auto, where runtime enables handshake only when it predicts improvement.
Phase 4: document and flip default to on after two weeks of stable telemetry and no high-severity numeric incidents.
During all phases: ops runbook for rollback, and automated alert if handshake success rate drops below 80% or if any model-level eval regression exceeds configured threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes quant_handshake config and handshake API contract is stable for handshake_v1.
Prototype kernels (attention + fused-ffn) implement handshake microhooks and pass unit tests for zero-copy and fallback modes.
End-to-end perf benchmark shows at least 10% decode-stage latency improvement on average for INT8/FP8 pipelines in staging.
No untriaged numeric regressions observed for models flagged strict-numeric over 72h canary window.
Telemetry emits handshake metrics (success_rate, avoided_materializations, avg_handshake_ms) and dashboards are created in Console.
Documentation for kernel authors and ops runbook published and linked from the PR.
